_comment: One row per signature the scanner (check_rules.py) runs and verify_rules.py resolves rule tags against; check_rules.flatten_signatures turns it into one list per platform. Shared fields, once per row: id (stable; approved deviations and exceptions cite it), rule (the rule id it holds), group (optional: several signatures held by one rule tag, e.g. native-pattern), kind ('builtin' names a check implemented in code rather than a regex), severity block|ratchet|advisory, scope added|tree, applies_to / excludes (path classes from paths.json; '*' = every class), once (report a file once, not per line), words (the failure's plain words). Under platforms, one entry per platform the signature runs on: files (optional glob list; default = the platform's extensions), files_excluded, pattern (regex over a line, and over the file's added lines joined without whitespace), paired (optional second regex that must also match), and any shared field the platform's value differs on (rule, words, applies_to …), which is laid over the row's. A signature absent from a platform is not listed there.

signatures.words: raw NSWindow/NSApplication reach-through from SwiftUI — window behavior belongs to SwiftUI's scene and window APIs
an NSViewRepresentable touching .window — a bridge view reaching into the hosting window's chrome
window-chrome override (standardWindowButton/styleMask/makeKeyAndOrderFront/titlebarAppearsTransparent) — replaces the platform's window controls
hiding the window toolbar (.toolbar(.hidden, for: .windowToolbar)) — removes the native title bar and traffic lights
a hand-rolled Route enum in place of NavigationStack — navigation belongs to the platform's navigation container
an AndroidView bridge into the View system from Compose — Compose's own components own the UI; a new bridge needs approval
a window-flags override — insets and system bars belong to the platform's edge-to-edge and WindowInsets APIs
overriding onBackPressed — back handling belongs to BackHandler / OnBackPressedDispatcher
a direct DOM query from component code — the framework's refs and state own the DOM
writing raw HTML into the page — content belongs to the framework's rendering (and raw HTML is an injection surface)
an element acting as a button — use <button>, which the platform makes focusable and keyboard-operable
a full-screen scrim/dimming overlay used as a modal — modals belong to .sheet/.popover/.alert

android.words: a dimming overlay used as a modal — dialogs and sheets belong to Dialog / ModalBottomSheet

react-native.words: an absolute-positioned dimming overlay used as a modal — modals belong to Modal

web.words: a fixed dimming overlay used as a modal — dialogs belong to <dialog> (showModal)

signatures.words: writing browser history by hand — routes belong to the app's router
a positive tabindex — focus order belongs to document order
a hand-built dropdown — a choice belongs to <select> (or the platform's popover)
a direct native-module reach-through — a platform feature React Native already exposes is used through its own API; a new native bridge needs approval
direct view manipulation (UIManager / findNodeHandle / setNativeProps) — the view belongs to React's render
a hand-rolled screen switch over mutable state — navigation belongs to the Navigation component (NavHost)

react-native.words: a hand-rolled navigator holding the current screen in state — navigation belongs to React Navigation

signatures.words: an NSEvent key monitor — key handling belongs to the platform's focus and command system
focus APIs used to override key handling — the platform's command/shortcut system owns keys
a custom header/title bar in a hidden-title-bar window — the window's native title bar and toolbar own the header; if the platform provides the feature, use the feature
a hand-built tab bar — tab navigation belongs to TabView, even when every piece of the substitute is a native control

android.words: a hand-built tab bar — tabs belong to NavigationBar / TabRow

react-native.words: a hand-built tab bar — tabs belong to the tab navigator

signatures.words: a hand-rolled search field (a TextField dressed with the search icon) — search belongs to .searchable
a hand-styled sidebar list — sidebars belong to NavigationSplitView, which provides the sidebar column and its styling itself
a hand-drawn progress indicator — progress belongs to ProgressView

android.words: a hand-drawn progress indicator — progress belongs to CircularProgressIndicator / LinearProgressIndicator

react-native.words: a hand-drawn progress indicator — progress belongs to ActivityIndicator

web.words: a hand-drawn progress indicator — progress belongs to <progress>

signatures.words: reaching into navigation internals — use the navigation hooks
reflection into platform internals — use the platform's public API
a custom-built control where the platform provides one (Picker/Slider/Stepper/Toggle) — use the native control

android.words: a custom-built control where the platform provides one (DatePicker/Slider/Switch/Checkbox) — use the native control

signatures.words: module layering: feature modules never import each other, only the app target imports Data, Domain imports nothing app-side
user-facing text written as a literal in view code — it belongs in the string catalog under a semantic key
a colour or font size written as a literal — every visual value is a token in the theme file
a spacing, size or radius written as a number — use the theme's spacing tokens
a second theme or tokens file — styling has one home, the bound theme file; a brand swap is a one-file edit
a fact about the world outside the code written as a literal (a branch, a path, a host, a port, a fallback) — ask the system that owns it or read the one configured home
a secret written into the tree (a key, a token, a private key, a password) — secrets live in the platform's secure store, never in source
a secret- or data-shaped file added to the tree (an .env file, a key, a certificate, a database) — it never enters version control
a plain http:// connection (or the setting that allows one) — every connection is HTTPS; a local dev server is the only exception and it is named in the config home
untrusted text rendered as raw HTML — it goes through the framework's escaping, or through a sanitizer, never straight into the page
input handed to eval, exec, pickle or an unsafe YAML loader — untrusted data is parsed by a parser that cannot run it
a command run through the shell — subprocesses take an argument list, never a string the shell interprets

a component exported to other apps with no permission guarding it — components are private unless they must be reachable, and a reachable one names its permission (the launcher activity is the one exception the pattern already knows)
a SQL statement assembled from a string — values are bound parameters, never pasted into the text
a script loaded from a URL at runtime — dependencies are installed and pinned by the lockfile; a CDN script changes under you
a call that parks a thread and waits — long waits are async/await; nothing that blocks is reachable from the main actor

android.words: a call that parks a thread and waits — long waits are suspend functions on a dispatcher; nothing that blocks runs on Main

react-native.words: a busy wait or a synchronous request on the JavaScript thread — long waits are promises the thread does not sit on

web.words: a busy wait, a synchronous request or a blocking dialog on the main thread — long waits are promises the thread does not sit on

python.words: a blocking call inside an async function — file and network I/O and sleeps go through the loop's async forms or run_in_executor

signatures.words: a data or network framework imported into view code — screens display; data goes through the repository layer

python.words: database access inside a handler — handlers call the data-access layer; the query lives there

signatures.words: a password hashed by hand with a general-purpose digest — the platform's password hasher (argon2/bcrypt through passlib, or the framework's make_password) owns it
a URL, query string or header taken apart by hand — urllib.parse and the framework's request object already own that
command-line flags parsed by hand from sys.argv — argparse owns the flags, the help text and the errors
a UI framework imported into a view model — view models prepare data and know nothing about the toolkit that draws it
a destructive action wired to the Return key or auto-focused — a destructive confirm is a deliberate click, never the default action
a plural chosen by hand with `count == 1` — plurals come from the catalog's plural variants, which know every language's rules
a sentence assembled by concatenation — text with values in it is one catalog entry with placeholders, because word order differs across languages
casing baked into the string in code — all-caps and capitals are a render-time style (a text-case modifier or CSS), because casing rules differ per language
a second strings catalog — every locale has one catalog in the bound strings home; a table beside it is a second place the same sentence can live
a catalog key that is an English sentence — keys name the meaning (`vehicle.status.doNotDispatch`), so a translation can diverge from the English
a font size fixed in points — text takes a Dynamic Type text style (or a custom font relative to one) so the system text-size setting applies

macos.words: a font size fixed in points — text takes a system text style so the text-size setting applies

android.words: a font size in dp — text is measured in sp so the system font-size setting applies

react-native.words: font scaling switched off — text follows the system text-size setting

web.words: a font size fixed in pixels — body text is measured in rem/em so browser text scaling applies

signatures.words: a screen-scale size fixed in code — layout adapts through the platform's layout system; fixed dimensions break on the next window size or device
a test that names no acceptance criterion — its name or its comment says which criterion it verifies (`AC-3`, or the word criterion)
a merge-gating test reaching a live service — tests fake their external dependencies locally; a live test is guarded by the LIVE_TESTS switch and never blocks a merge
a test skipped, disabled, focused or asserting nothing — tests are honest: a failing test is fixed or the task stays open, never quieted
a log line that names a personal or secret field — personal data never reaches logs, analytics or crash reports; log the event, not the value
a comment trailing the code on the same line — the name says what the code does; a comment is for the why, on its own line, only when the why is not obvious
the word "guarantee" — a legal word Coast never uses; say protections, enforcement or safeguards
a type or file grown past the size one job needs — a signal for the reviewer to ask whether it has taken on a second job
a money field typed as binary floating point — money is a decimal or a whole number of the smallest unit, because floats cannot hold cents exactly
a public declaration with no doc comment — every public type and function says what it does, or the generated API reference has nothing to render
